title: Platform Foundation & Security Lab
description: Enter the SOC environment, inspect devices, navigate the course roadmap, track progress, and run your first safe labs.

lessons.title: Welcome to the Security+ Zero-to-Hero Platform

title: Computer, Network & Security Foundations
description: How computers, operating systems, and networks actually work — and where the security controls sit. Everything later in the course attaches to this path.

lessons.title: Computers, Operating Systems and Processes
The Command Line on Windows and Linux
Networking Foundations — TCP/IP, Addressing, DNS and DHCP
Network Devices, Secure Protocols and the Connection Path

labs.title: Identify Listening Ports and Attack Surface

title: Security Fundamentals
description: The vocabulary every later phase reuses: CIA, AAA, the security principles, the language of risk, and the control taxonomy. Precision here is what separates a finding that gets funded from one that gets ignored.

lessons.title: The CIA Triad and the AAA Model
Security Principles — Least Privilege, Defence in Depth, Zero Trust
The Language of Risk
Security Controls and Their Two Axes

labs.title: Map Defence in Depth to a Real Asset

title: Threats, Vulnerabilities & Attacks
description: The largest exam domain at 22%. Malware, social engineering, password attacks, and attack categories across the estate — taught as recognition and defence, with every technique described by the evidence it leaves and the control that catches it.

lessons.title: Malware — Classifying by Propagation and Behaviour
Social Engineering and the Phishing Family
Password Attacks and Insider Threats
Attack Categories Across the Estate
The Attack Chain — Putting It Together

labs.title: Walk the Attack Chain End to End

title: Security Architecture
description: The topology the earlier phases have been implicitly describing. Zones and segmentation, the boundary controls that enforce them, Zero Trust and NAC, deception, and the resilience that makes availability a security property.

lessons.title: Segmentation, VLANs and Security Zones
Boundary Controls — Firewalls, IDS, IPS, WAF and Proxies
Trust, Access and Deception — Zero Trust, VPN, NAC, Honeypots
Secure Architecture, Redundancy and High Availability

labs.title: Review the Architecture for Resilience and Deception

title: Identity & Access Management
description: The major career component. Identity as the control plane, authentication factors and why not all MFA is equal, federation protocols, directory services and Kerberos, authorisation models, and the joiner-mover-leaver lifecycle you will spend your career operating.

lessons.title: Identity and the AAA Model in Practice
Authentication Factors, MFA and Password Policy
SSO, Federation, SAML, OAuth and OpenID Connect
Directory Services — LDAP, Active Directory and Kerberos
Authorization Models — RBAC, ABAC, Least Privilege and PAM
The Identity Lifecycle and Non-Human Identities

title: Cryptography & PKI
description: The machinery underneath everything earlier phases relied on. Four operations that get constantly confused, symmetric and asymmetric cryptography, hashing and signatures, and the certificate trust chain that makes TLS possible.

lessons.title: Encryption vs Hashing vs Encoding vs Signing
Symmetric Encryption and the Key Distribution Problem
Asymmetric Encryption, RSA, ECC and Key Exchange
Hashing in Practice — SHA-256, Salting, HMAC and Signatures
PKI, Certificates and the TLS Handshake

labs.title: Distinguish Encryption, Hashing, Encoding and Signing
Certificates, PKI and the Trust Chain

title: Security Operations / SOC
description: The largest exam domain at 28%, and where every earlier phase converges. The SOC toolchain, the log sources, alert triage and the false positive problem, and a full investigation of the intrusion this platform has carried since Phase 0.

lessons.title: The SOC Toolchain — SIEM, EDR, XDR and SOAR
Reading the Log Sources
Alert Triage and the False Positive Problem
Threat Intelligence, IOCs and IOAs

labs.title: Know Your Tools and Your Logs

title: Windows Security
description: The platform most enterprises actually run. Accounts and the privilege model, NTFS permissions, Defender and firewall, the logging settings that are off by default, and the persistence mechanisms that make an incident recur.

lessons.title: Accounts, Groups and the Windows Privilege Model
NTFS Permissions and the Share Interaction
Defender, Firewall and Endpoint Controls
Event Viewer, Sysmon and PowerShell Logging
Services, Scheduled Tasks, Registry and Persistence

labs.title: Create Users and Groups in an Isolated Lab

title: Linux Security
description: The counterpart to Windows Security, asking the same questions in a different dialect. Users and sudo, permissions and the special bits, SSH hardening, systemd and persistence, logs and auditd — closing with an explicit mapping between the two platforms.

lessons.title: Users, Groups and sudo
File Permissions and the Special Bits
SSH, Services and systemd
Linux Logs, auditd and Secure Configuration

title: Vulnerability Management
description: Finding weaknesses systematically rather than by hand. CVE and CVSS, scan types and why false positives happen, verification before reporting, and prioritisation by real exposure rather than by the number the scanner printed.

lessons.title: Vulnerabilities, CVE and CVSS
Vulnerability Scanning, False Positives and Verification
Prioritisation, Remediation and Validation

labs.title: Verify Findings and Eliminate False Positives

title: Network Security
description: Building and securing an enterprise network on the Phase 4 zone architecture. Firewall rule order and shadowing, VLAN segmentation and its failure modes, IDS and IPS placement, wireless and NAC, and the DHCP and DNS controls that close on-path attacks.

lessons.title: Firewalls, ACLs and Rule Order
Segmentation, VLANs and Monitoring
Wireless, NAC, VPN and Infrastructure Services

title: Incident Response
description: The seven-phase lifecycle, evidence handling and order of volatility, and containment judged on two axes — stopping the attacker and preserving the evidence. Closes the incident this platform has carried since Phase 0.

lessons.title: The Incident Response Lifecycle
Evidence, Volatility and Containment
Incident Types and the Response Report

labs.title: Work the Lifecycle and Handle Evidence
Close the Incident and Write the Report

title: Threat Intelligence
description: Turn artifacts into actionable intelligence: intelligence lifecycle, IOC/IOA, Pyramid of Pain, ATT&CK mapping, threat actor types, feed quality, STIX/TAXII, and Admiralty Code.

lessons.title: Intelligence Lifecycle and Feed Quality
From IOCs to TTPs – Building Durable Detections

labs.title: Classify Indicators and Map the Incident

title: Cloud Security
description: Master cloud service models, the shared responsibility boundary, Cloud IAM, security groups, logging, encryption, container and serverless security, API protection, and secrets management — then audit a simulated cloud environment for misconfigurations.

lessons.title: Cloud Service Models & Shared Responsibility
Cloud-Native Risks & Modern Workloads

title: Mobile / IoT / Embedded Security
description: Master mobile device ownership models, MDM/MAM, mobile application and OS security, then move to IoT and embedded systems: default-credential risk, firmware lifecycle, device identity, and network segmentation — and design a secure enterprise IoT network.

lessons.title: Mobile Security & Device Management
IoT & Embedded Device Security

labs.title: Design a Secure Enterprise IoT Network

title: Application & Data Security
description: Master secure application development (shift left, input validation, authentication vs authorisation, OWASP Top 10), then data security: classification tiers, data states, DLP, tokenization vs masking vs encryption, and retention — applied to a simulated vulnerable application and data inventory.

lessons.title: Secure Application Development
Data Security & Protection

labs.title: Find and Fix Injection & Access Control Vulnerabilities

title: Governance, Risk & Compliance
description: Master the risk management cycle (risk register, ALE, treatment), the policy/standard/procedure/guideline hierarchy, and security awareness, then compliance frameworks, audits, third-party vendor risk, and business impact analysis — applied to a simulated risk assessment for a fictional company.

lessons.title: Risk Management & Governance
Compliance, Audits & Third-Party Risk

title: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
description: Master BCP vs DR, RTO/RPO, MTTR/MTBF, backup strategies and the 3-2-1 rule, high availability, then alternate site selection, BC/DR testing, and disaster-specific recovery design for ransomware, server, network, and cloud outages.

lessons.title: BC/DR Fundamentals & Metrics
Recovery Sites, Testing & Disaster Scenarios

labs.title: Calculate Recovery Objectives and Choose a Recovery Site
Design Recovery Plans for Four Disaster Scenarios

title: Security Hardening
description: Consolidate and extend endpoint and network hardening: cross-platform control categories, patch management as a process, PowerShell security controls, Linux service/MAC hardening, network attack surface reduction, centralised AAA, ACL design, and a secure, segmented management plane — applied to a deliberately insecure mixed environment.

lessons.title: Cross-Platform Endpoint Hardening
Network & Infrastructure Hardening

labs.title: Harden a Windows and Linux Endpoint Baseline

title: Security Automation
description: Master Python and JSON fundamentals for security scripting, regex-based log parsing, secure API credential handling, and SOAR concepts, then apply them to the core automation projects: failed-login detection, IOC extraction, automated report generation, threat-intelligence API querying, and evidence collection with chain of custody.

lessons.title: Python & Automation Fundamentals for Security
Building Security Automation Projects

labs.title: Parse Authentication Logs and Detect Failed Login Patterns
Automate a Security Report and Query a Simulated API

title: Wireshark & Packet Analysis
description: Master reading a packet capture: ARP, ICMP, TCP (flags and the three-way handshake), UDP, DNS, DHCP, HTTP, and TLS, then apply that skill to identify protocols, follow full conversations, find suspicious traffic (ARP spoofing, DNS tunnelling, cleartext credentials, SYN floods), and explain the evidence.

lessons.title: Packet Capture Fundamentals: ARP, ICMP, TCP, UDP
Application-Layer Protocols & Following Conversations

labs.title: Identify Protocols and Follow a TCP Conversation
Find Suspicious Traffic and Explain the Evidence

title: Security Troubleshooting Center
description: Investigate ten realistic security scenarios through a structured, eight-panel investigation interface — diagnosing root cause and recommended action from evidence rather than instinct.

lessons.title: Structured Security Troubleshooting
Recognising the Ten Common Alert Categories

labs.title: Investigate a Compromised Account Using the Investigation Interface
Diagnose All Ten Troubleshooting Center Scenarios

title: Full SOC Capstone
description: Work a second full incident — an enterprise ransomware event via a compromised vendor VPN account — through detect, triage, investigate, collect evidence, contain, remediate, recover, and document, across the full enterprise topology.

lessons.title: The Full Attack Chain, End to End
Ransomware Response and the Order-of-Volatility Exception

labs.title: Detect, Triage, Investigate, and Collect Evidence

title: Security+ Exam Preparation
description: Build and use an exam-preparation toolkit: domain-scoped quizzes, weak-area review, adaptive sessions, and full timed mock exams with a weighted scaled score and readiness verdict.

lessons.title: Reading a Question Like the Exam Wants You To
Building a Study Plan From Your Own Data

labs.title: Run a Weak-Area Review and a Full Mock Exam

title: GitHub Cybersecurity Portfolio
description: Turn completed labs into professional, consistently structured GitHub repositories, then curate and index a role-targeted portfolio across every domain this platform covers.

lessons.title: What Makes a Security Portfolio Repo Credible
Building the Portfolio, Lab by Lab

labs.title: Generate and Review a Professional Lab Repository

title: Career Mode
description: Map a target role's job description to Security+ concepts, run a gap analysis against your own mastery data, rehearse interview and troubleshooting questions, and recommend portfolio projects — while never fabricating professional experience.

lessons.title: From Job Description to Study Plan
Interview Readiness and Professional Honesty

labs.title: Map a Job Description to a Targeted Study Plan
Rehearse Interview Questions and Check Portfolio Honesty

title: Security+ to IAM Career Bridge
description: Connect every relevant Security+ concept to how identity is actually implemented, logged, and investigated — authentication, authorization, MFA, SSO, RBAC, Zero Trust, privileged access, identity telemetry, and IAM incident containment — then meet the vendor platforms, gated behind the concepts they implement.

lessons.title: How Security+ Identity Controls Are Actually Implemented
Zero Trust, Privileged Access, and IAM Incident Investigation

labs.title: Trace an Identity Incident Across Three Log Sources
Map Vendor Features Back to the Concepts They Implement
